heroHeadline: Day 380: India's Airspace NOTAM Expires Without Renewal Announcement — Back-Channel Signals Sustain Quiet Diplomatic Track
heroSubtitle: May 25, 2026: India's NOTAM banning Pakistani aircraft from Indian airspace reached its May 24 expiry date without a formal public renewal announcement, leaving the bilateral airspace arrangement in de facto ambiguity. Pakistan's reciprocal ban continues through June 23/24. The back-channel meetings revealed by Al Jazeera on May 23 — four informal India-Pakistan contacts since the ceasefire in London, Muscat, Bangkok, and Doha — have elicited no official Indian response but continue to generate strategic discussion. India's MEA reiterated the Indus Waters Treaty will remain suspended until Pakistan takes 'credible and irreversible steps to end terrorism support,' as the IWT legal dispute continues following India's 'null and void' rejection of the PCA's May 15 award. The ceasefire holds at Day 380 — no LOC incidents, no ambassadors, $0 formal trade.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
